from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Review: Concrete Base established.",
            "Visual Linkage created.",
            "Logical Boundaries checked.",
            "Encourage building mental maps.",
            "Master your mathematical explanation."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Summary & Application: The 3-Step Checklist", lecture_lines)
        
        # Elements
        box_style = {"color": YELLOW, "stroke_width": 2}
        
        # 1. Concrete Base
        check1 = Square(side_length=0.4, **box_style)
        text1 = Text("1. Concrete Base", font_size=20, color=YELLOW)
        group1 = VGroup(check1, text1).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.3)
        self.place_at_grid(group1, 'B2', scale_factor=1.2)
        
        # 2. Visual Linkage
        check2 = Square(side_length=0.4, **box_style)
        text2 = Text("2. Visual Linkage", font_size=20, color=YELLOW)
        group2 = VGroup(check2, text2).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.3)
        self.place_at_grid(group2, 'C2', scale_factor=1.2)
        
        # 3. Logical Boundaries
        check3 = Square(side_length=0.4, **box_style)
        text3 = Text("3. Logical Boundaries", font_size=20, color=YELLOW)
        group3 = VGroup(check3, text3).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.3)
        self.place_at_grid(group3, 'D2', scale_factor=1.2)

        # Mascot representation
        mascot = Circle(radius=0.5, color=BLUE).set_fill(BLUE, opacity=0.5)
        mascot_text = Text("Checklist Owl", font_size=16, color=WHITE)
        mascot_group = VGroup(mascot, mascot_text).arrange(DOWN)
        self.place_at_grid(mascot_group, 'E5', scale_factor=1.0)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        self.play(Create(group1))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        self.play(Create(group2))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        self.play(Create(group3))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[3].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        self.play(FadeIn(mascot_group))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[4].animate.set_color(YELLOW))

            group1.animate.set_stroke(width=5),
            group2.animate.set_stroke(width=5),
            group3.animate.set_stroke(width=5),
            Indicate(VGroup(group1, group2, group3))

sections.title: Introduction: The 'Why' of Clarity
sections.content: A brief hook explaining that math is a language. Effective explanation isn't just about truth; it's about transmission. We define the goal: minimizing cognitive load while maximizing conceptual retention.
sections.example: Comparing a messy, text-heavy manual vs. an intuitive IKEA-style graphic assembly guide for a robot.

sections.title: Criterion 1: The Principle of Gradual Abstraction
sections.content: Introduce prerequisite knowledge mapping. Never jump to symbols before building a concrete mental model. Use visual animations to show transitions from 'Physical Object' to 'Geometric Model' to 'Algebraic Formula'.
sections.example: Explaining the concept of Area: Start with counting square blocks on a grid, then move to a rectangle shape, finally arriving at the formula A = l × w.

sections.title: Criterion 2: Visual-Spatial Encoding
sections.content: Discuss the 'Dual Coding Theory'. Explanations must pair verbal descriptions with spatial representations. Use animation to highlight how a graph 'breathes' when a variable in a function changes.
sections.example: Visualizing the Sine function: An animation of a 'Math-Cat' running around a circle, with the y-coordinate being plotted simultaneously on a Cartesian graph to the right.

sections.title: Criterion 3: The 'So-What' Connection
sections.content: Ensure every mathematical concept is grounded in a logical sequence. Use a 'Constraint Check': Does the audience understand the limitations and valid ranges of the concept?
sections.example: When teaching division by zero, use an animation of a hungry 'Robo-Chef' trying to distribute 10 cookies into 0 jars. Show the system error visual to emphasize the logical boundary.

sections.title: Summary & Application: The 3-Step Checklist
sections.content: Conclude with a summary checklist for any explanation: 1. Concrete Base (Prerequisites), 2. Visual Linkage, 3. Logical Boundaries. Encouraging the creation of a 'Mental Map' for students.
sections.example: The 'Checklist Mascot': An owl icon that appears on screen summarizing: [Anchor to Reality] -> [Visual Translation] -> [Boundary Check].
